newsitem.title: USA: Orange & Rockland defends N.Y. retail power pilot.
newsitem.headline: Orange & Rockland defends N.Y. retail power pilot.

text.p: Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc defended itself Tuesday against early criticism of its trial program to allow selected retail customers to buy electricity from outside suppliers.
The program, called PowerPick, is a bid by the company to test electricity sales in the deregulated power market mandated by New York State.
While satisfied overall with PowerPick, launched in July, participants said their savings were less than anticipated.
"It's not perfect. We expect to gain a lot of knowledge," (from PowerPick)," Larry Brodsky, president of Orange & Rockland, told an energy symposium hosted here by the utility.
Based on early data, PowerPick participants saved 17.36 percent on their electricity bills, Brodsky said.

If transmission, ancillary and back-up service charges were included, their savings were whittled down to about five percent, said David Fazzino, vice president of Minolta Advanced Technologies and a PowerPick participant.
"You won't save on transmission costs," Fazzino said.
But O&R Chief Executive Officer D. Louis Peoples said the cost of transmission and support services the utility charges in the program are justified.
"They exist to support the service we provide...(though) improvements could be made," Peoples said.
Other criticism heard at the symposium included O&R's failure to fully explain the intricacies of the program and that it used confusing industry jargon.

At least one participant, IBM who was represented by regional program manager Carl DiGregorio, said it was also displeased with an arrangement that automatically shares all power savings of 10 percent or more with the utility to help it pay down regulatory costs.
The pilot program initially allowed electricity producers outside O&R's service territory to sell up to 30 megawatts of power to 10 participating commercial customers.
The program was expanded in August to include 1,500 randomly selected New York state residential customers.
-- R Leong, New York Power Desk + 1 212 859 1622
